assumptions: Continues the original loaded launch/deployment/deorbit state below its descending 90 km witness on physical body flaps and distributed (Jorgensen crossflow) aerodynamics. Hypersonic angle of attack 59.5 deg, calibrated against the broadcast descent displays (residuals +1.2/+1.3/+0.6 km at T+10369/10541/10961, speed 7291 vs 9982 km/h at the last, 1.2 km reached about 7 s before the broadcast); half a degree below the 60-70 deg belly-first band a secondary source reports, and very sensitive (57 deg reaches 1.2 km 100 s late); in the distributed model lift/drag is about cot(alpha), so the former 55 deg experiment glided far too high. Attitude feedback on the physical flaps is gain-scheduled (0.3 rad/s, damping 0.8) by the flaps' full-command angular authority. The angle of attack moves to an 80 deg terminal belly flop between 250 and 130 m/s; an onboard trim limiter (the vessel's own hull and flap model) never commands an angle the flaps cannot trim with 15 deg of travel to spare, and a reference governor keeps the attitude reference within 6 deg of the actual attitude. Bank-limited hypersonic corridor: max(20 m/s, 0.006 x airspeed) downward with a 20 s response and 30 m/s deadband. Controls, thresholds and the endpoint are engineering estimates, not measured Flight 14 commands. No forces, state, fuel or thermal values are imposed.
